summary: An in-process scheduled-task runner: tasks every interval or daily at HH:MM in a chosen zone, with an injected Clock, busy-slot skip, permit limit, panic recovery and a bounded Stop.
use_when: a job must run every N minutes or hours inside a long-running service
a task, such as a nightly cleanup, must run once a day at a fixed time of day (03:30, say), read in a chosen time zone
a scheduled background task must not pile up: it skips a slot while its previous pass is still going, survives a panic and stops within a bound at shutdown
schedule code must be tested by driving a fake clock instead of waiting
not_for: scheduling across replicas or distributed locking: it is in-process only, so two replicas both run a task unless the task claims its slot itself
cron expressions or calendars: only a fixed interval and a daily HH:MM exist
a durable job queue or retries with backoff: a slot missed while the process is down is not replayed
